topic: Model Context Protocol — current spec (revision 2026-07-28) as of August 2026
executive_summary:
Current protocol version is the exact string `2026-07-28` (`LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION = "2026-07-28"` in schema.ts; docs.json labels it "Version 2026-07-28 (latest)"). Prior revisions, in order: `2024-11-05`, `2025-03-26`, `2025-06-18`, `2025-11-25`. The version strings are the dates. Sources fetched from a shallow clone of modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol at commit 4df2d6b (2026-08-14).

2026-07-28 is the largest breaking revision to date. MCP is now STATELESS: `initialize`/`notifications/initialized` are gone, `Mcp-Session-Id` is gone, SSE resumability (`Last-Event-ID`) is gone. Every request carries `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"]` and `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities"]`. `server/discover` replaces the handshake and is MUST-implement. `subscriptions/listen` (a long-lived POST-response SSE stream) replaces the HTTP GET endpoint and `resources/subscribe`.

Critically for AiKi: server-initiated requests no longer exist. Sampling, elicitation, and roots/list are now delivered via **MRTR** — the server returns `InputRequiredResult` (`resultType:"input_required"`) with an `inputRequests` map plus an opaque, integrity-protected `requestState`; the client re-issues the ORIGINAL request with a NEW JSON-RPC id carrying `inputResponses` + `requestState`. Elicitation for spend approval works, but as a retry loop, not a callback.

Long-running work: Tasks were REMOVED from core and are now the official extension `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks`, specified in github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-tasks — which is still marked `draft` and explicitly "under development". Shape is complete and buildable (`CreateTaskResult` with `resultType:"task"`, `tasks/get` polling, `tasks/update`, `tasks/cancel`, `ttlMs`/`pollIntervalMs`, statuses working|input_required|completed|failed|cancelled). It can carry a minutes-to-days job lifecycle, but you are betting on a pre-release extension.

Auth is OAuth 2.1 + RFC 9728 PRM (MUST) + RFC 8707 resource indicators (MUST) + RFC 9207 `iss`; RFC 7591 DCR is now DEPRECATED in favor of Client ID Metadata Documents.

findings.claim: Current protocol version string is exactly `2026-07-28`; prior revisions are `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26`, `2024-11-05`.
findings.detail: `schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts:30` contains `export const LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION = "2026-07-28";`. `schema/draft/schema.ts:30` contains the same value, i.e. draft has not yet advanced past the released revision. `docs/docs.json:29` and `:401` read `"version": "Version 2026-07-28 (latest)"`. Version directories present under both `schema/` and `docs/specification/`: 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25, 2026-07-28, plus `draft`. Note 2025-06-18 has a schema+spec dir but the 2026-07-28 changelog says the previous revision is 2025-11-25. Revision dates ARE the version strings; the spec does not publish separate release dates. Repo HEAD at time of research: commit 4df2d6b6e3588efb46e7542d98498e5c630a0a86, dated 2026-08-14. SPEC.

findings.claim: MCP is now stateless: `initialize` handshake, `Mcp-Session-Id`, `ping`, `logging/setLevel`, and SSE resumability are all REMOVED in 2026-07-28.
findings.detail: Changelog major changes 1, 2, 5, 9. Protocol-level sessions and the `Mcp-Session-Id` header are removed from Streamable HTTP (SEP-2567); list endpoints no longer vary per-connection. Servers needing cross-call state use "explicit, server-minted handles passed as ordinary tool arguments." The `initialize`/`notifications/initialized` handshake is removed (SEP-2575); every request carries `_meta` keys `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` (required), `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities` (required), `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo` (SHOULD). Servers SHOULD return `io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo` in each result's `_meta`. Version mismatch → `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError` code `-32022` with `data:{supported:[...],requested:...}`. `Last-Event-ID` and SSE event IDs are removed: "A broken response stream loses the in-flight request; clients MUST re-issue it as a new request with a new request ID." Log level is per-request via `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel"]`; servers MUST NOT emit `notifications/message` for requests lacking it. SPEC.

findings.claim: Transports defined: stdio and Streamable HTTP. HTTP+SSE (2024-11-05) is formally Deprecated. There is no separate "stateless mode" — the whole protocol is stateless now.
findings.detail: `docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/` contains only `stdio.mdx` and `streamable-http.mdx` (plus index). Streamable HTTP: server MUST provide a single MCP endpoint path supporting POST (e.g. `https://example.com/mcp`). Every JSON-RPC message from the client is its own HTTP POST. Client MUST include an `Accept` header listing both `application/json` and `text/event-stream` (server MUST support both response forms). Body MUST be a single JSON-RPC request or notification; client MUST NOT send JSON-RPC responses. Notification POST accepted → `202 Accepted` with no body. Server MUST validate `Origin`; invalid present Origin → error response. Server SHOULD send `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on SSE. For long-lived streams servers are encouraged to emit SSE comment keep-alives (`:\r\n`). Closing the SSE response stream MUST be treated by the server as cancellation of that request. Resumable SSE via `Last-Event-ID` is not supported. SPEC.

findings.claim: Streamable HTTP now REQUIRES routing headers `MCP-Protocol-Version`, `Mcp-Method`, and (for tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get) `Mcp-Name`.
findings.detail: Every POST to the MCP endpoint MUST include `MCP-Protocol-Version` (e.g. `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28`). Its value MUST match `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"]`; mismatch → server MUST reject with `400 Bad Request` (schema error `HEADER_MISMATCH = -32020`). Unsupported version → `400 Bad Request` with `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError`. Standard headers table: `Mcp-Method` ← `method`, all requests; `Mcp-Name` ← `params.name` or `params.uri`, on `tools/call`/`resources/read`/`prompts/get`. If the `Mcp-Name` source cannot be safely represented as plain ASCII, clients MUST encode it using a Base64 sentinel format. Tool input-schema properties may carry an `x-mcp-header` annotation that mirrors an argument value into an HTTP header; use by servers is optional but conforming clients MUST honor annotations that are present. A server implementing only 2026-07-28 rejects a legacy `initialize` POST with `400 Bad Request` per server validation. SPEC.

findings.claim: LONG-RUNNING WORK: Tasks exist but were moved OUT of core into the extension `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks`, whose spec repo is still marked draft/under-development.
findings.detail: Changelog major change 6: "Move experimental tasks out of the core protocol and into an official extension (`io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks`). The redesigned extension replaces the blocking `tasks/result` method with polling via `tasks/get` and a new `tasks/update` for client-to-server input, removes `tasks/list`, and allows servers to return task handles unsolicited without per-request opt-in" (SEP-2663). Spec lives at github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-tasks. That repo's README states: "This repository is under development and is working towards implementing the changes described in SEP-2663." Only `specification/draft/tasks.md` and `schema/draft/schema.ts` exist — no dated release directory. ext-tasks HEAD commit 2c1425d, 2026-07-15, i.e. it predates the core 2026-07-28 release and still cites the OLD error code `-32003` for MissingRequiredClientCapability, which core renumbered to `-32021`. Treat the extension as buildable-but-moving. SPEC (draft).

findings.claim: Task lifecycle: 5 statuses, poll-first with optional notifications, cooperative cancellation, mutable TTL — sufficient to carry a minutes-to-days job.
findings.detail: `TaskStatus = "working" | "input_required" | "completed" | "failed" | "cancelled"`. `completed`/`failed`/`cancelled` are terminal. Server responds to a supported request with `CreateTaskResult` = `Result & Task`, `resultType: "task"`. Server MUST NOT return `CreateTaskResult` to a client that did not include the extension capability on that request (error `-32003` per ext-tasks draft / `-32021` per core). Server MUST NOT return `CreateTaskResult` until the task is durably created — a `tasks/get` for the taskId would resolve; in eventually-consistent environments the server MUST wait for consistency. `ttlMs: number | null` (null = unlimited) is measured from `createdAt` and MAY change over the task's life; servers MAY mark a task `failed` any time after TTL elapses and delete it thereafter; clients MAY treat TTL as a backstop. `pollIntervalMs` is a hint clients SHOULD honor; servers MAY rate-limit faster pollers. `tasks/cancel` is cooperative and eventually consistent — the task may still reach a non-`cancelled` terminal status. `notifications/cancelled` MUST NOT be used for task cancellation. SPEC (draft).

findings.claim: Task transport routing: `tasks/get`, `tasks/update`, `tasks/cancel` MUST set `Mcp-Name` to `params.taskId` on Streamable HTTP.
findings.detail: Verbatim from ext-tasks/specification/draft/tasks.md line 511: "When `tasks/get`, `tasks/update`, or `tasks/cancel` is sent over the Streamable HTTP transport, the client MUST set the `Mcp-Name` header to the value of `params.taskId`. This allows transport intermediaries and load balancers to route subsequent requests for the same task to the server instance holding its state, which is typically required for correctness. The `Mcp-Method` header is set to the JSON-RPC method name per standard header conventions." Also: `notifications/progress` and `notifications/message` MUST NOT be sent on the `subscriptions/listen` stream for a task, and "are not supported on tasks in general in this specification" — so progress reporting on a long AiKi job must go through `statusMessage` on the Task object, not progress notifications. Task status push uses `notifications/tasks` carrying a full `DetailedTask`, subscribed via `subscriptions/listen` with `taskIds?: string[]`. SPEC (draft).

findings.claim: ELICITATION: schema unchanged in substance (form + url modes), but delivery changed completely — servers can no longer send `elicitation/create` as a request. It must be embedded in an `InputRequiredResult` (MRTR) or in a Task's `inputRequests`.
findings.detail: MRTR page, verbatim: "Servers MUST send server-to-client requests (such as `roots/list`, `sampling/createMessage`, or `elicitation/create`) using the MRTR pattern. The previous pattern of server-initiated requests is no longer supported. This is a breaking change." `ElicitRequestFormParams`: `mode?: "form"`, `message: string`, `requestedSchema: {$schema?, type:"object", properties: {[k]: PrimitiveSchemaDefinition}, required?: string[]}` — only top-level primitives (StringSchema/NumberSchema/BooleanSchema/EnumSchema), no nesting. `ElicitRequestURLParams`: `mode: "url"` (required), `message`, `url` (format uri). `ElicitResult`: `action: "accept"|"decline"|"cancel"`, `content?: {[k]: string|number|boolean|string[]}` present only when accept+form. 2026-07-28 REMOVED `notifications/elicitation/complete` and the `elicitationId` field of URL-mode elicitation (both added in 2025-11-25); servers correlate across retries by encoding their own identifier in `requestState`. SPEC.

findings.claim: MRTR `requestState` is an attacker-controlled opaque blob; servers MUST integrity-protect it and SHOULD bind principal, TTL, and originating request.
findings.detail: `InputRequiredResult` fields: `resultType: "input_required"`, `inputRequests?` (map, keys server-assigned and unique within the request; values MUST be one of ElicitRequest | CreateMessageRequest | ListRootsRequest), `requestState?` (opaque string). Server MUST include at least one of the two. Server MUST NOT send an inputRequest type the client did not declare in capabilities. Client MUST echo `requestState` byte-exact on retry and MUST NOT inspect/parse/modify it; the retry MUST use a DIFFERENT JSON-RPC id. Only `prompts/get`, `resources/read`, and `tools/call` may return `InputRequiredResult`; servers MUST NOT return it on any other request. Security: "servers MUST treat `requestState` as an attacker-controlled input… MUST protect its integrity (e.g. HMAC or AEAD) and MUST reject state that fails verification." SHOULD embed inside the protected payload: the authenticated principal, a short expiry, and an identifier for the originating request (method + digest of salient params). Explicit warning that these bound the replay window but do NOT guarantee single-use — one-time redemptions MUST be enforced server-side. SPEC.

findings.claim: AUTHORIZATION: OAuth 2.1 draft-13, RFC 9728 PRM is MUST for servers, RFC 8707 resource indicators are MUST for clients, RFC 9207 `iss` is SHOULD-emit/MUST-validate. RFC 7591 DCR is now DEPRECATED.
findings.detail: Normative refs: OAuth 2.1 draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-13; RFC 8707 Resource Indicators; RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata. MCP server = OAuth 2.1 resource server; MCP client = OAuth 2.1 client. Servers MUST implement RFC 9728; clients MUST use PRM for AS discovery. Auth servers MUST provide at least one discovery mechanism and clients MUST support both. 401 carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://mcp.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"` and SHOULD carry `scope`; clients MUST treat challenged scopes as required for the current request and MUST NOT assume any set relationship with `scopes_supported`. `resource` MUST be sent in BOTH authorization and token requests, MUST identify the MCP server, MUST be the canonical URI, and MUST be sent regardless of whether the AS supports it. Servers MUST validate tokens were issued specifically for them as audience per RFC 8707 §2; invalid/expired → HTTP 401. Servers MUST only accept tokens valid for their own resource and MUST NOT accept or transit any other tokens. Authorization header MUST be on every HTTP request; tokens MUST NOT appear in query strings. SPEC.

findings.claim: Client registration: Client ID Metadata Documents (URL-as-client_id) is the preferred mechanism; RFC 7591 DCR remains only for backwards compatibility and now requires `application_type`.
findings.detail: Priority order: use an out-of-band/pre-registered client_id if available; else Client ID Metadata Documents if the AS advertises `client_id_metadata_document_supported: true` in AS metadata; else DCR. CIMD per draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document-00: client MUST host metadata at an HTTPS URL; the `client_id` URL MUST use https scheme AND contain a path component (e.g. `https://example.com/client.json`); document MUST include at least `client_id`, `client_name`, `redirect_uris`; the `client_id` value MUST match the document URL exactly. Clients MAY use `private_key_jwt` with JWKS. Authorization servers SHOULD fetch metadata on URL-formatted client_ids, MUST validate client_id==URL, MUST validate the presented redirect_uri against the document, MUST validate JSON structure/required fields. DCR path: clients MUST specify an appropriate `application_type` (avoids OIDC redirect-URI conflicts, SEP-837); clients MUST key persisted credentials by issuer identifier, MUST NOT reuse them with a different AS, and MUST re-register when the AS changes (SEP-2352). SPEC.

findings.claim: Tool definition: `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` now accept ANY JSON Schema 2020-12 keywords; `structuredContent` is now any JSON value, not just an object.
findings.detail: `Tool extends BaseMetadata, Icons` with `description?`, `inputSchema: {$schema?: string; type: "object"; [key:string]: unknown}`, `outputSchema?: {$schema?: string; [key:string]: unknown}`, `annotations?: ToolAnnotations`, `_meta?`. Root `type:"object"` is still required on inputSchema; beyond that any 2020-12 keyword may appear — `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf`/`not`, `if`/`then`/`else`, `$ref`/`$defs`/`$anchor`. Defaults to 2020-12 when `$schema` is absent (SEP-2106 also added `$ref` resolution requirements and composition-keyword resource bounds). `CallToolResult`: `content: ContentBlock[]` (required), `structuredContent?: unknown` ("any JSON value… that conforms to the tool's outputSchema if one is defined"), `isError?` (tool-originated errors SHOULD be reported here with `isError:true`, NOT as protocol errors, so the LLM can see them). `ToolAnnotations` are hints only: `title?`, `readOnlyHint?` (default false), `destructiveHint?` (default TRUE), `idempotentHint?` (default false), `openWorldHint?` (default TRUE). Display name precedence: `title` → `annotations.title` → `name`. SPEC.

findings.claim: Roots, Sampling, and Logging are DEPRECATED as of 2026-07-28 (SEP-2577), with a minimum twelve-month removal window.
findings.detail: Changelog Deprecated §1: "Deprecate the Roots, Sampling, and Logging features (SEP-2577). These features remain fully functional during the deprecation window but new implementations should not add support for them. Suggested migrations: pass directories or files via tool parameters, resource URIs, or server configuration instead of Roots; integrate directly with LLM provider APIs instead of Sampling; log to `stderr` (stdio) or use OpenTelemetry instead of Logging." The `roots` and `sampling` fields of `ClientCapabilities` carry `@deprecated Deprecated as of protocol version 2026-07-28 (SEP-2577)` in schema.ts, as do `LoggingMessageNotification`/`LoggingMessageNotificationParams` and `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel"]`. A new feature-lifecycle policy defines Active/Deprecated/Removed states with a minimum twelve-month deprecation window and a deprecated-features registry at `/specification/2026-07-28/deprecated`. Sampling's `includeContext` values `"thisServer"`/`"allServers"` are Deprecated; use `"none"` or omit. HTTP+SSE transport reclassified Deprecated. SPEC.

findings.claim: Pagination is unchanged (opaque cursor), but all list/read results now REQUIRE `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` via the new `CacheableResult` interface.
findings.detail: Pagination: opaque `cursor` string, no numbered pages; page size is server-determined and clients MUST NOT assume a fixed size. Response carries optional `nextCursor`; client continues by sending `params.cursor`. New in 2026-07-28 (SEP-2549): `CacheableResult extends Result` with required `ttlMs: number` (minimum 0; 0 = immediately stale; positive = fresh for that many ms, semantics analogous to HTTP `Cache-Control: max-age`) and required `cacheScope: "public" | "private"` ("public" = no user-specific data, any intermediary MAY cache and serve across authorization contexts; "private" = cacheable only within the same authorization context, MUST NOT be shared across authorization contexts — a different access token requires a different cache). Applies to `tools/list`, `prompts/list`, `resources/list`, `resources/read`, `resources/templates/list`, and `server/discover` (`DiscoverResult extends CacheableResult`). Servers SHOULD return tools from `tools/list` in a deterministic order for client caching and LLM prompt-cache hits. SPEC.

findings.claim: Error model: standard JSON-RPC codes plus a new allocation policy partitioning the server-error range; three new MCP codes at -32020/-32021/-32022.
findings.detail: From schema.ts: `PARSE_ERROR = -32700`, `INVALID_REQUEST = -32600`, `METHOD_NOT_FOUND = -32601`, `INVALID_PARAMS = -32602`, `INTERNAL_ERROR = -32603`, `HEADER_MISMATCH = -32020`, `MISSING_REQUIRED_CLIENT_CAPABILITY = -32021`, `UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION = -32022`. Allocation policy (changelog minor §12): `-32000`..`-32019` remains implementation-defined (existing SDK usage grandfathered); `-32020`..`-32099` reserved for the MCP specification. Codes introduced earlier in this draft were renumbered: HeaderMismatch -32001→-32020, MissingRequiredClientCapability -32003→-32021, UnsupportedProtocolVersion -32004→-32022. Resource-not-found changed from `-32002` to `-32602` (Invalid Params) to align with JSON-RPC. `Error` object is `{code: number, message: string, data?: unknown}`; message SHOULD be a concise single sentence. Tool-execution failures belong in `CallToolResult.isError`, not in a protocol error. SPEC.

findings.claim: RATE LIMITING is essentially unspecified. No 429/Retry-After semantics anywhere in the 2026-07-28 spec.
findings.detail: A grep for `rate limit|Rate Limit|429|Retry-After` across the whole of `docs/specification/2026-07-28/` returns exactly three hits, all soft SHOULDs in unrelated pages: progress.mdx:89 "Both parties SHOULD implement rate limiting to prevent flooding"; completion.mdx:212 "Implement appropriate rate limiting"; sampling.mdx:672 "Clients SHOULD implement rate limiting". There is no `429` mention, no `Retry-After` header semantics, no backoff algorithm, and no error code for throttling. The only structured throttling primitives in the whole surface are (a) `CacheableResult.ttlMs` as a polling-reduction hint and (b) the Tasks extension's `pollIntervalMs`, where ext-tasks says "Servers MAY rate-limit clients polling more frequently than the recorded `pollIntervalMs`" — but defines no signalling for it. A production remote MCP server must define its own throttling contract out-of-band or via implementation-defined codes in the grandfathered `-32000`..`-32019` range. SPEC (by absence).

findings.claim: `server/discover` is the replacement for `initialize` and is MUST-implement; `subscriptions/listen` is the sole long-lived notification channel.
findings.detail: `DiscoverResult extends CacheableResult` with `supportedVersions: string[]`, `capabilities: ServerCapabilities`, and `instructions?: string` ("Natural-language guidance describing the server and its features… should focus on information that helps the model use the server effectively and should not duplicate information already in tool descriptions"). Servers MUST implement it; clients MAY call it first or MAY go straight to any RPC and handle `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError`. On stdio it doubles as the legacy/modern era probe. `SubscriptionsListenRequest` = `{method:"subscriptions/listen", params:{notifications: SubscriptionFilter}}`; the server MUST NOT send notification types the client did not explicitly request. Opt-in filters named in the changelog: `toolsListChanged`, `promptsListChanged`, `resourcesListChanged`, `resourceSubscriptions` (plus `taskIds` from the Tasks extension). The server tags every notification on that stream with `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId"]` = the JSON-RPC id of the listen request. `resources/subscribe` and `resources/unsubscribe` are removed. Extensions are negotiated via a `capabilities.extensions` map on both sides. SPEC.

findings.claim: OpenTelemetry trace context propagation is now a documented `_meta` convention.
findings.detail: Changelog minor change 2: "Document OpenTelemetry trace context propagation conventions for `_meta` keys (`traceparent`, `tracestate`, `baggage`) (SEP-414)." `_meta` key naming rules: any prefix whose second label is `modelcontextprotocol` or `mcp` is reserved for MCP use — `io.modelcontextprotocol/`, `dev.mcp/`, `org.modelcontextprotocol.api/`, `com.mcp.tools/` are all reserved; `com.example.mcp/` is NOT reserved because the second label is `example`. Extension identifiers MUST follow the same rules with a mandatory prefix. Request `_meta` also still carries `progressToken?: ProgressToken` (string|number) for `notifications/progress`, which on Streamable HTTP flows on the response SSE stream of the originating request only — not on the `subscriptions/listen` stream, and not at all for Tasks. SPEC.

tasks/get, tasks/update, tasks/cancel, notifications/tasks
Result / ResultType / CacheableResult / PaginatedResult

Tool + ToolAnnotations + CallToolResult

UnsupportedProtocolVersionError + MCP error code constants

interfaces.name: Extension negotiation + DiscoverResult

gaps: Exact CALENDAR release dates for each revision were not found as separate metadata — the spec publishes only the date-shaped version strings (2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25, 2026-07-28) as directory names and LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION. I did not locate a page listing 'revision X was published on date Y' distinct from the string itself.

modelcontextprotocol.io was unreachable from this environment (ECONNREFUSED on 76.76.21.21:443). All findings come from the GitHub repos, which are the upstream source for that site; I could NOT independently confirm the live site currently serves 2026-07-28 at /specification/latest. docs.json labels 2026-07-28 '(latest)' and defines the /specification/latest redirect, which is strong but indirect evidence.

The Tasks extension has NO released/dated version. github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-tasks contains only specification/draft/ and schema/draft/, and its README says the repo 'is under development'. Its HEAD (2026-07-15) predates core 2026-07-28 and still references error code -32003, which core renumbered to -32021. Field names could still move before an ext-tasks release.

I did not read server/tools.mdx, server/resources.mdx, server/prompts.mdx, client/roots.mdx, or client/sampling.mdx in full. Resources, prompts, and roots details beyond what appears in the changelog, schema, and pagination pages are unverified — in particular resource URI templates, resource annotations/priority, prompt argument completion semantics, and the full ContentBlock union.

No spec text on rate limiting beyond three soft SHOULDs. There is no 429 status, no Retry-After semantics, and no throttling error code anywhere in the 2026-07-28 spec. Any throttling contract for a remote server is entirely out of scope of the standard.

Whether major clients (Claude, VS Code, Cursor, etc.) have actually SHIPPED 2026-07-28 support is not covered here. docs/extensions/client-matrix.mdx exists in the repo but I did not read it; DEPLOYED client support is unverified.

x-mcp-header validity/extraction rules: I saw the annotation referenced in Tool.inputSchema docs and the transport section heading, but did not read the full 'Schema Extension' subsection defining which header names are permitted or how conflicts are resolved.
Whether MCP defines anything about payments, x402, or onchain settlement: not investigated. No evidence either way was encountered while reading the 2026-07-28 tree.

ServerCapabilities full shape and the SubscriptionFilter type body were not read verbatim; filter names (toolsListChanged, promptsListChanged, resourcesListChanged, resourceSubscriptions) come from the changelog prose, not from the TypeScript definition.
aiki_implications: MCP can carry a full minutes-to-days job lifecycle, but ONLY via the Tasks extension, and that extension is pre-release. Build the AiKi job lifecycle behind your own interface and treat io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks as one adapter. Core MCP alone can only INITIATE work — with sessions, initialize, and SSE resumability all removed, there is no core mechanism for a result that outlives a single HTTP request/response.

Tasks map cleanly onto AiKi's model: tools/call returns CreateTaskResult{taskId, status:'working', ttlMs, pollIntervalMs}; the client polls tasks/get. Server MUST NOT return the task handle until the task is durably created — 'in eventually-consistent environments, the server MUST wait for consistency before responding.' That is a hard write-before-ack requirement on your job store. Plan for a synchronous durable insert on the hot path.

ttlMs is a soft, mutable contract, not a guarantee: 'servers MAY mark a task as failed at any point after the TTL elapses, and subsequently delete it at any time.' For day-scale jobs set a large or null ttlMs and re-advertise it on each tasks/get. Do not rely on the client to hold state — persist taskId → job → onchain settlement mapping yourself, keyed by authenticated principal.

SPEND APPROVAL: elicitation works but the delivery model inverted. Servers can no longer push elicitation/create. Either (a) return InputRequiredResult with mode:'form' or mode:'url' and have the client retry the whole tools/call, or (b) inside a Task, move to status:'input_required', surface inputRequests on tasks/get, and receive the answer via tasks/update. Option (b) is right for AiKi: approval arrives on a separate RPC without re-running the tool.

requestState is the single highest-risk surface for an agent-commerce platform. The spec is explicit that it is attacker-controlled and MUST be HMAC/AEAD-protected, with principal binding, short TTL, and an originating-request digest embedded inside the protected payload. And it warns that this does NOT guarantee single-use — 'Servers for which a given requestState must be consumed at most once (e.g., one-time redemptions) MUST enforce that invariant server-side.' A spend approval IS a one-time redemption. You need a server-side nonce table; the protocol will not stop replay of a spend authorization.

For URL-mode elicitation (the natural fit for a wallet-signature or BNB Chain approval page), note that 2026-07-28 REMOVED elicitationId and notifications/elicitation/complete. Correlation between your approval page and the pending call is now entirely your problem: encode your own correlation id inside requestState (MRTR) or key it to taskId (Tasks).

Per-user auth for a remote AiKi MCP server is fully specified and non-optional: serve /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (RFC 9728, MUST), emit WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=... with a scope hint on 401, and validate that every token's audience is YOUR canonical resource URI per RFC 8707. 'MCP servers MUST only accept tokens that are valid for use with their own resource... MUST NOT accept or transit any other tokens' — you cannot forward a user's AiKi token to a downstream merchant MCP server. Each hop needs its own audience-scoped token.

Prefer Client ID Metadata Documents over RFC 7591 DCR for any AiKi-authored client: DCR is now formally deprecated. Advertise client_id_metadata_document_supported: true on your AS if AiKi issues tokens. Also implement RFC 9207 iss on authorization responses now — the spec says a future revision will upgrade it from SHOULD to MUST.

Statelessness is a gift for horizontal scale but removes per-connection identity. Since list endpoints 'no longer vary per-connection', a marketplace whose tool list depends on the calling user must vary tools/list by the OAuth token instead — and MUST then set cacheScope:'private' on that result, or a shared gateway will leak one merchant's tool list to another user. Getting cacheScope wrong is a cross-tenant data leak, not a perf bug.

Progress reporting for long jobs is constrained. notifications/progress flows only on the response SSE stream of its originating request, and ext-tasks states notifications/progress and notifications/message 'are not supported on tasks in general in this specification.' For a days-long AiKi job, the only sanctioned progress channel is Task.statusMessage observed via tasks/get polling, or notifications/tasks pushed over subscriptions/listen.

If you front AiKi with a load balancer, honor the routing headers: Mcp-Method on every POST, Mcp-Name = params.name/params.uri, and specifically Mcp-Name = params.taskId on tasks/get|update|cancel — the spec says this is 'typically required for correctness' so intermediaries can pin a task to the instance holding its state. Design your job store as shared/durable anyway so this stays an optimization rather than a correctness dependency.

Do not build on Sampling or Roots. Both are Deprecated as of 2026-07-28 with a 12-month minimum window; the spec's own migration advice is to integrate directly with LLM provider APIs and to pass paths as tool parameters. For an AiKi marketplace, expose capability through tools + resources + prompts only.

Model tool failures correctly for a commerce audit trail: business failures (insufficient balance, merchant declined) belong in CallToolResult.isError = true so the model can see and react; only protocol violations should be JSON-RPC errors. If you mint custom codes, the -32000..-32019 range is implementation-defined and safe; -32020..-32099 is now reserved for the spec and will collide.

Budget for a dual-era server if you want reach today: the compatibility matrix says a Legacy client against a Modern-only server simply FAILS with no fall-forward. Serving both an initialize handshake and modern per-request _meta on the same endpoint is explicitly permitted and is the only way to onboard clients that have not shipped 2026-07-28.

Rate limiting is a spec vacuum — no 429, no Retry-After, no error code. For a paid marketplace you must define and document your own throttling contract, and use pollIntervalMs (which servers MAY enforce) plus CacheableResult.ttlMs as the only standards-blessed levers to shape client load.
